headers.before: Munhee (26) is a young noblewoman, being attended by her low-rank servants.
headers.label: Coronation Morning
headers.why: map/place opener → household dressing; nothing tells the reader this is the crowning day until block 27

headers.before: Bupmin is six. He finds his father and uncle on the hill
headers.label: The Hill
headers.why: dressing room → the hill above the palace; cast changes (Yushin appears)

headers.before: Before they dress for the hall he takes the two of them
headers.label: The Palace Road
headers.why: hill → horseback ride on the palace road

headers.before: King Jinpyung (65) is dead, after years of expanding Silla
headers.label: The Throne Hall
headers.why: family ride → the hall, bone ranks, the three princesses

headers.before: I put on this confident face,
headers.label: Before the Crown
headers.why: hall exposition → private Sunduk/Yushin moment; reader needs to know it is before the crowning, not after

headers.before: The capital’s daughters follow the Sword of Silla around the yard.
headers.label: The Yard
headers.why: coronation/hall → Hwarang yard, court maids watching Yushin

headers.before: Then the young knights kneel and pledge themselves to the throne.
headers.label: The Pledge
headers.why: yard/private exchange → back to the coronation ceremony

headers.before: Silla sends envoys to the other kingdoms to let them know
headers.label: The Envoys
headers.why: Surabol → Sabi, Pyongyang, Chang'an in four lines with no break

headers.before: He sends her a gift: a painting of peonies in three colours
headers.label: The Peonies
headers.why: Tang court → back in Surabol with Sunduk reading the gift

headers.before: Long after the stones are mossed over, the old men of the capital
headers.label: After the Wine
headers.why: the king's reign → old men generations later; time and cast both jump

headers.before: On the crown prince’s day, the court chalks a square grid
headers.label: The Sand
headers.why: ten clan term cards → the tourney Prince Euija left mid-reading; reusing Prince Euija's last header label signals the same day continues

headers.before: The Satek clan is currently the most powerful.
headers.label: The Assembly
headers.why: yard at dusk → clan politics at the Rock; no longer the tourney

headers.before: The Yunbi boys turned a Satek cart over at the west bridge yesterday.
headers.label: The West Bridge
headers.why: Assembly elders → street gossip about the feud

headers.before: A month before the Summit, in a Mohe village
headers.label: The Burned Village
headers.why: outpost yard → a Mohe village a month earlier; place and time both jump

headers.before: Years later, on the north wall of Pyongyang
headers.label: The North Wall
headers.why: flash-forward years ahead to Pyongyang; unmarked

headers.before: The summons isn't addressed to him.
headers.label: The Summons
headers.why: flash-forward → back to the present at the Eastern Command with Yeon Taejo

headers.before: In the yard the Eastern banners answer him anyway
headers.label: The Palace Yard
headers.why: Summit chamber → yard with Dosuryu and the crowd

headers.before: At dusk he gathers the flower youth under the eaves
headers.label: Under the Eaves
headers.why: daytime yard → dusk recital; Sadaham's frame is set here, so the place must be named

headers.before: Gotaso (16) goes out to the lantern market with two maids
headers.label: Two Springs Earlier
headers.why: opener → abduction two years back; also fixes the age confusion if the (16) is corrected

headers.before: They find the road on the second night.
headers.label: The Ford
headers.why: household → the ford two nights later

headers.before: Before the wedding, there is a year that nobody writes down
headers.label: The Gyuku Match
headers.why: rescue → spring gyuku stands, a different year and a different story

headers.before: They meet again under the flowering trees behind the training ground
headers.label: The Flowering Trees
headers.why: gyuku stands → secret meetings behind the training ground

headers.before: Rain finds them once on the palace steps.
headers.label: The Palace Steps
headers.why: flowering trees → palace steps, a later day

headers.before: …My lady. Your hands are cold.
headers.label: The Wedding Night
headers.why: wedding hall → bridal chamber

headers.before: The hall empties. The Queen does not leave, and neither does the Marshal.
headers.label: The Empty Hall
headers.why: bridal chamber / Daeya departure → back in the wedding hall with Sunduk and Yushin

headers.before: Outside the hall, two lantern-sellers argue
headers.label: Outside the Hall
headers.why: Sunduk/Yushin → street outside, new cast

headers.before: Five days later Yushin brings a young nobleman home
headers.label: The Torn Coat
headers.why: sisters selling a dream → Yushin's yard with Chunchu five days later

headers.before: Yushin builds the pyre in the yard where they played gyuku
headers.label: The Pyre
headers.why: courtship → the public pyre and Sunduk on the terrace; months later

headers.before: The complaint reaches the High Commander’s table
headers.label: The Uncle’s Supper
headers.why: Taehak courtyard → Gusesa's supper table

headers.before: He walks the riverbank the morning after the dragon
headers.label: The Morning After
headers.why: small-wonders montage → next morning on the bank

headers.before: At the Rock of Politics he arrives last
headers.label: The Rock
headers.why: riverbank → the Rock with the ministers

headers.before: Two court maids attend him
headers.label: The King’s Chamber
headers.why: the Rock by day → private chamber at night

headers.before: That winter, the Assembly's loud fight isn't about war.
headers.label: The Assembly
headers.why: private audience with Yunchung → open Assembly with the clans

headers.before: Silla’s ambush is waiting.
headers.label: The Night Road
headers.why: months of campaign summary → one night on the road to the prince's camp

bridges.en: Back in the yard, the Queen has forgotten to look away.
bridges.ko: 다시 마당. 여왕은 눈을 돌리는 걸 잊었다.
bridges.why: after the boyhood flashback, Yushin's 'Are you feeling alright, your majesty?' lands with no place; the reader cannot tell if this is the yard, the hall or before the crowning

bridges.en: Then the names start. Somebody always tries a man first.
bridges.ko: 이제 이름들이 오간다. 누군가는 꼭 남자 이름부터 꺼낸다.
bridges.why: blocks 12, 14, 15 are unattributed council voices written as narration; the reader can't tell who is talking or that the debate has begun

bridges.after: The smallest seat on the rock, and the hardest to buy.
bridges.en: Back to the sand, where the herald has just finished reading.
bridges.ko: 다시 모래판. 전령이 막 이름을 다 읽었다.
bridges.why: Prince Euija ends mid-tourney; ten term cards stall it, and block 12 restarts the crown prince's day as if new

bridges.after: The Yunbi boys turned a Satek cart over at the west bridge yesterday.
bridges.en: Back on the rock, the two elders are still at it.
bridges.ko: 다시 바위 위. 두 어른은 아직도 그 싸움이다.
bridges.why: street gossip → the elders trade lines again with no place

bridges.after: His Majesty wants Samhan under one roof.
bridges.en: That night a rider finds him. His wife's time has come.
bridges.ko: 그날 밤 전령이 그를 찾는다. 아내의 해산이 시작됐다.
bridges.why: yard → birth chamber; the header alone doesn't say why Yeon is suddenly at a birth

bridges.after: A border post with a fine view of Baekje.
bridges.en: But that is days off. Tonight the hall is still lit.
bridges.ko: 하지만 그건 며칠 뒤 일이다. 오늘 밤 전각엔 아직 불이 켜 있다.
bridges.why: the couple have already left for Daeya, then the next block is back in the wedding hall the same night

bridges.after: The Legend of the Hwarang — Bidam — still sits at one hundred and eight
bridges.en: Earlier that evening, the feast had a stranger at its edge.
bridges.ko: 그날 저녁 일찍, 잔치 가장자리에 낯선 이가 있었다.
bridges.why: after the empty hall and the street, Haesang appears 'at the feast's edge' — the feast is over; jump back unmarked

bridges.after: By midsummer the household staff have stopped announcing him.
bridges.en: Ask Munhee about the next part and she still blushes.
bridges.ko: 그다음 이야기를 물으면 문희는 지금도 얼굴이 붉어진다.
bridges.why: next block is Munhee in the present frame ('why bring up that memory again'), cutting out of the flashback with no marker

bridges.after: Yushin invites him back onto the gyuku field.
bridges.en: By autumn Munhee is showing. Chunchu still hasn't proposed.
bridges.ko: 가을이 되자 문희의 배가 불러 온다. 춘추는 아직 청혼을 안 했다.
bridges.why: Yushin's 'Pregnant, with no husband to name' arrives with no setup for the pregnancy or Chunchu's delay

bridges.after: Your Majesty — is this the country you mean to hand the princes?
bridges.en: Gyebek steps forward. Nobody asked him to.
bridges.ko: 계백이 앞으로 나선다. 아무도 시키지 않았다.
bridges.why: Euija answers 'No, Gyebek… not you' to a Gyebek who has not spoken or moved; Seongchung's question is left hanging

stories.logline: The last woman of the bone wants to know she can be king; a court that hates the word 'woman' and her own feeling for Yushin stand in the way; the turn is Yushin asking her to say his name once before titles take over; she is crowned, then reads Taizong's scentless peonies and wins the first round by reading people.
stories.fixes: Too many openings before the heroine: Munhee's hair, the hill, the palace ride and the bone lecture all come before Sunduk speaks at block 25. Keep 'A Queen? Ridiculous.', then cut the family material to one beat (Bupmin's 'no bone' line). Order is broken: the 'last day for it' name exchange (42–53) happens after she is crowned (30) and after the yard ogling. Move 34–53 (Yushin intro, yard, east-star flashback, name exchange) before block 30, so the crowning lands on 'Your Majesty. Nothing else.' Block 6 says 'two children' but block 3 already has Inmun, so there are three. Block 11 has Munhee on the hill, though she was last seen at her hair. Block 50 ('last time in forty-one years that anyone calls him that') is contradicted by Pumsuk, where Sunduk says 'Yushin.' again. The envoy montage (61–73) should end on the peonies, which are her best beat. Move Jomei's line before the peony gift, then the name hanja and the card.

stories.logline: Six nobles must agree on a king by dawn and three refuse a woman; the youngest, Bidam, stands up out of turn; Alchun's tiger line turns the last hand; six to nothing, and Bidam and Yushin go back to their 108-all rivalry.
stories.fixes: A tight single-room scene. It needs: (1) the council members (Murim, Imjong, Suljong, Yumjang) speak with no introduction. One narrator line seating the six would help. (2) The count is off: seven men speak (Bidam, Yushin and the five elders), but the text says six sleeves. Make Bidam the seventh, or drop one. (3) The Lotus Sutra dragon-girl quote (29) floats after the vote. Put it right after Bidam's speech, or cut it. (4) The tiger quote retells Alchun's line, which breaks the 'one telling per event' rule. Keep one.

stories.logline: The Cloud King makes Silla big with stones and a yard of boys, then shaves his head; the old men still can't decide if 'cloud' is praise.
stories.fixes: This is an essay, not a story. Nobody wants anything on the page, and the herald/elder voices are anonymous. Give it one scene: Jinheung at a stone with the herald, or the day he shaves his head with the court still saying Majesty. The Hwarang paragraphs (8–12) can carry a line from that scene. Handoff in and out is good. The elder's 'Gwansan' tease sets up The Severing well; don't explain it further here.

stories.logline: Five days before he is made crown prince, Euija needs a champion who belongs to no clan; an eel boy with no name dives five days for a Jinmo burner; the prince saves him from the river, steals his father's crown to summon the deer, names him Buyeo Gyebek and puts him on the sand.
stories.fixes: Benchmark. Minor: the closing 'Five days' recap flashback (111) repeats lines the reader just heard and could be cut. The last card hands straight into the tourney, so Eight Great Clans must pick up on the sand without restarting the day (see that entry).

stories.logline: The eight houses fight over the king's sons and the river berths; on the crown prince's day their boys fight it out on chalk and sand, and Gyebek outlasts the Jinmo boy; nothing is settled, and Elder Satek turns his thumb down for reasons he never explains.
stories.fixes: Handoff problem. Prince Euija ends with the herald reading names and 'Eight boys on the sand'. This episode opens with Heewon's clan roll (keep it), then ten term cards, then block 12 restarts 'On the crown prince's day' as if it were a new day. Move the term cards (3–11) down into the Assembly section and go from the roll straight to the sand. Block 12 refers to 'the west bridge', which isn't mentioned until block 39; plant it first or cut the reference. Block 22 still calls Gyebek 'the crown prince's nobody' after Prince Euija named him on that same sand. Say 'Buyeo Gyebek', or 'the eel boy with the royal name'. Make his bout the climax and end the tourney there. The Rock term and diagram are repeated in King Euija and Yunchung. Keep one telling (Yunchung, where it matters) and trim the Assembly half here to the Satek/Yunbi feud. Better last beat: the unexplained thumb (47), but only if it pays off later. If it never fires, cut it.

stories.logline: Baekje's thirteenth king marches north and a Goguryeo king dies on his own wall; the chant 'restore the thirteenth' is born.
stories.fixes: No scene, two quotes for the same arrow (3 and 4), and a third quote about the Seven-Branched Sword. Keep one quote and dramatize one moment: the stray arrow on the Pyongyang wall seen from the Baekje side, or the crown prince handing over the sword. Block 9 spends King Euija's 'a country is a story' line and says it 'gets Daeya burned', which spoils the Daeya arc. Soften it to a tease. The handoff in (from Eight Great Clans) and out (to Commander Yeon) works.

stories.logline: Yeon holds the frontier by terror and builds a wall; he takes in a Mohe boy who guards a burned house and names him Gulgul; his father hands him the seal and sends him to Pyongyang with one instruction, 'say half'.
stories.fixes: Biggest order bug in the range. The traitor is asked 'Do you know what happens to traitors' (4), executed (5), and then interrogated again with the same question (11–13) after he is dead. Move 11–13 to replace 4 and keep the execution after them. Block 14 says 'A month before the Summit', but the Summit isn't introduced until the summons at 36. Change it to 'a month before the summons', or move the summons earlier. The heart of the episode is Gulgul. The North Wall flash-forward (30–35) is lovely but needs its header. The summons should come back as the last scene so 'say half' sets up the next card. 'Manchuria' is a modern word; 'the high mountains of the north' is better.

stories.logline: Yeon wants the court ready for the Second Emperor; five commanders and his uncle want to split a granary; threatened with the word 'traitor', he walks out to a cheering yard; that night his first son is born.
stories.fixes: The council fight works and has real moves. The Namseng birth is tacked on: it needs the bridge, or should move to open Academy. Blocks 35 and 37 read like image prompts ('no extra bodies, no portrait-frame crowd', 'The portrait does not stay paint'). Rewrite them as storyteller narration. The opener lecture (3–7: quote, term, diagram, table) delays Yeon's entrance. Bring 'Pyongyang already knows the sound of those hooves' up against the chamber noise.

stories.logline: Silla begs Goguryeo for help, the Great King's horsemen clear the Wa, and then stay for fifty years.
stories.fixes: Essay. Blocks 2 and 3 repeat each other ('sixty-four fortresses… the stele'), and the Stele episode will say it again. Dramatize the Silla king's begging letter, or the horsemen riding into Surabol and not leaving. The strongest idea is the tease in block 9: a Silla prince will one day ask a foreign emperor for an army. The last card then pivots to Bupmin's Hwarang rules, which has nothing to do with it. Either point the card at Bupmin through 'what Silla never forgets', or move this episode next to Chunchu's Tang mission.

stories.logline: At fifteen Bupmin trains under his uncle; Yushin asks which of the five rules he will break first; the boy who always pulls up behind his sister answers 'retreat', meaning he refuses to be only a follower.
stories.fixes: The ending works, but the middle is world-building: clubs, cypress, handicaps (9–12). Cut most of it, or give it to a character with a want. Plant Bupmin's want early: he is tired of following Gotaso and his father. The 'retreat' answer then pays it off. The 641 jump from Gwanggaeto is abrupt. The opener is fine, but the map/diagram could follow the first scene.

stories.logline: Under the eaves Yushin tells the new boys about two first-class friends who swore 'one dies, the other follows'; Mugwan dies of a cough and Sadaham keeps the swear by not eating for seven days.
stories.fixes: A strong frame tale, and the flashbacks are well marked. Drop the Yamato Mimana quote (16) and keep only the gate quote, which Yushin then waves away. The boys' frame interjections are good. The card into Gotaso works.

stories.logline: A girl who does what she wants falls for showy Pumsuk at a gyuku match and names their four children before he has asked her father; first, a prologue in which her father goes silent and does something unwritten at a ford to get her back.
stories.fixes: Two stories. The abduction is Chunchu's story: it plants his rage at losing his one daughter, and it is the better half. The romance has no obstacle, since everyone is on her side. Either give the romance resistance (Munhee doubts Pumsuk's flash; Pumsuk's rank), or open on the gyuku match and move the abduction to Pumsuk as Chunchu's reason for the vow. Ages: 'two springs earlier' still says (16), and the gyuku match says (16) again. The monologue at block 5 has no speaker. Is it Chunchu, from later? Mark it. Munhee speaking on the nineteen-li walk home (19) implies she rode out too; set that up.

stories.logline: Gotaso marries Pumsuk after Chunchu makes him swear on his life; while the newlyweds leave for the border, the Queen and Yushin stay in the empty hall and almost say it.
stories.fixes: The title is Pumsuk, but the spine is Sunduk and Yushin, and the opener (0) recaps Gotaso instead of hooking. Open on the vow ('If anything happens to her, you know I'm going to kill you'). Chronology bounces three times: Daeya departure (22) → back in the hall (24) → outside (55) → back to the feast (57). Move 22–23 to just before the closing card, and move Haesang (57–59) before the empty hall, or cut him. The girl-child flashback (10) reads like an image prompt. Sunduk's 'Your son's girl' is wrong (Chunchu is not her son), and 'that doorway has taken three' and Chunmyung's 'Four' are unreadable. Explain them or cut them.

stories.logline: Munhee buys her sister's dream for a skirt, mends Chunchu's torn coat, and keeps him; when she is pregnant and he still hasn't proposed, Yushin lights a pyre where the Queen can see it, and Chunchu shouts 'It's me!'; they marry, Bupmin is born, and Chunchu puts down his star.
stories.fixes: The best comic engine in the range (dream sale → torn coat → pyre) is buried by the 'Closed Months' section (46–63), which runs eighteen blocks and repeats the same beat. Trim it to two or three. The frame break at 28 needs the bridge. Before the pyre, plant Chunchu's delay and the pregnancy. Bupmin's birth says 'Years later', which is wrong; it is the next year. Block 68 ('Chunchu stopped going to the hill') contradicts Queen Sunduk, where six-year-old Bupmin finds him on the hill. Pick one.

stories.logline: Yeon marches his eldest to school in his boots, says the sutra can be skipped because the monks own the farms, and makes an enemy of a sweeping monk and his own uncle.
stories.fixes: Namseng's want ('be told he did well') is set up and never paid off. End on him reading his father's unopened Daodejing, and add one line where he hopes Yeon notices. Bodeok is a Chekhov plant; make sure he fires later. Stele (10 blocks) and Dosuryu (18 blocks) are fragments of the same Yeon household. Consider merging Academy + Stele + Dosuryu into one episode: school, rock, boots, list.

stories.logline: Yeon shows his sons the Great King's sixty-four fortresses and asks how that country now bows to Chang'an.
stories.fixes: A single beat with three quotes. Fold it into Academy as its closing scene, or into Dosuryu as the opener ('the boots' line then lands in the same house). Cut one of the two Tang tribute quotes (7 and 8).

stories.logline: Dosuryu walks in with his boots on to warn Yeon that the king and his uncle mean to kill him by spring; Yeon laughs, stops, and decides to make a longer list.
stories.fixes: A sharp single scene, but too slight to stand alone. Merge it with Stele/Academy. Keep one of the two 'the plan leaked' quotes (11 and 12), not both. The last line is the right cliffhanger.

stories.logline: Crowned at last, Euija fakes a dragon and a run of cheap miracles to own the country's story; Gyebek refuses to call paper a dragon and Seongchung asks what happens when the people find out; at the feast he sends his quiet son Pung away as a hostage.
stories.fixes: Three detours dilute it: the court-maid chamber scene (48–59), the nation chant (60), and the Gyebek age note (61). Keep the maids to one beat. Block 47 ('it is the sentence that kills him… word for word') follows narration, so the reader can't tell which sentence. Name it ('Nobody inspects the evidence…'). The 'general' card at 9 conflicts with 61 ('passed over every season'). The name 'Rock of Politics' here vs 'Rock of Government' in Eight Great Clans should be unified. A better last beat already exists: Pung asking 'For how long?'

stories.logline: Euija wants his country back off the Rock without a civil war; Yunchung says 'win a war abroad'; Euija sells the Assembly a crisis story and sends Yunchung with ten thousand men to Daeya.
stories.fixes: The title character vanishes after block 10 and returns for two lines at the end. Put Yunchung in the Assembly scene and let him be the one who says 'Daeya' (from the frontier he knows). The Rock quote and diagram (18–19) repeat King Euija and Eight Great Clans; keep only one. Gyebek's 'not you' exchange needs setup (bridge). Yunchung's 'Then we're done for, plain and simple' (44) reads as defeatism right before he promises Daeya by autumn. Clarify (does he mean 'then it's settled'?). Euija's long run of single-speaker lines (22–27, 35–42) breaks the 'someone should interrupt' rule; let Chunbok or Seongchung cut in once.

stories.logline: King Seong loses the river to his own ally, marches to take it back, rides out at night to steady his son, and is caught in a ditch where a slave takes his head on the Cloud King's order.
stories.fixes: Strong. Two cautions. (1) Muryuk's mystery box: the text doesn't name him, but the speaker id 'muryuk' on dialogue blocks 15 and 21 may render his name as the speaker label in the UI. Check that, and use an unnamed label until his episode. (2) Kingsung's 'A prince of Geumgwan' gives away nearly everything. Make it just 'Gaya…?'. The Hamsan quote (8) can go. The handoff in (Gyebek's 'What is the Severing') and out (Gumil card) works.
